es: Comprobar si el relato de una entrevista es fiel a las preguntas originales y detectar cuándo omite, exagera o distorsiona.

teaching.en: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even if the words change.
teaching.es: Un informe fiel mantiene el significado de la pregunta original, aunque cambien las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Fiel no es copiar: es conservar el sentido.
segments: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the
original question, even if the words change.
teaching.audioText: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even if the words change.

teaching.en: The panel did not challenge his answer; it only asked for an example, so Tom should not distort what happened.
teaching.es: El comité no cuestionó su respuesta, solo pidió un ejemplo, así que Tom no debería distorsionar lo ocurrido.
teaching.explanationEs: Challenge es poner en duda; pedir un ejemplo no lo es. Distort cambia el sentido.
segments: The panel did not challenge his answer; it only asked
for an example, so Tom should not distort what happened.
teaching.audioText: The panel did not challenge his answer; it only asked for an example, so Tom should not distort what happened.

teaching.en: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked if he could work at weekends only in summer.
teaching.es: No omitas la condición: el comité preguntó si podía trabajar los fines de semana solo en verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Omit: dejar fuera un dato; aquí la condición only in summer cambia la pregunta.
segments: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked if
he could work at weekends only in summer.
teaching.audioText: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked if he could work at weekends only in summer.

teaching.en: Saying that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate what happened; they only asked him to think.
teaching.es: Decir que el comité exigió una respuesta sería exagerar lo ocurrido: solo le pidieron que pensara.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerate convierte una pregunta en una exigencia: sube el grado.
segments: Saying that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate
what happened; they only asked him to think.
teaching.audioText: Saying that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate what happened; they only asked him to think.

teaching.en: An accurate report uses a precise verb: the panel may ask, enquire or press for details.
teaching.es: Un informe preciso usa un verbo exacto: el comité puede preguntar, indagar o insistir pidiendo detalles.
teaching.explanationEs: Ask es neutro; enquire about introduce un tema; press añade insistencia.
segments: An accurate report uses a precise verb: the
panel may ask, enquire or press for details.
teaching.audioText: An accurate report uses a precise verb: the panel may ask, enquire or press for details.

prompt.es: ¿El informe es fiel a la pregunta original?

choices.text: No, it changes the question type.
Yes, it keeps the meaning and moves the tense back.
No, it adds a condition.

feedback.es: Did you enjoy…? pasa a whether I had enjoyed…: misma pregunta de sí o no y tiempo retrocedido.

hint.es: Compara qué se pregunta y cómo retrocede el tiempo.

origin.text: Original: Did you enjoy the course? Report: They asked me whether I had enjoyed the course.

choices.text: It omits the date.
It changes the person.
It exaggerates: a question becomes a demand.

feedback.es: El original es una pregunta (Can you…?) y el informe dice demanded: sube el grado y la convierte en una exigencia.

hint.es: Mira si «preguntar» se ha convertido en algo más fuerte.

origin.text: Original: Can you start in June? Report: They demanded that I start in June.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preguntaron si podía empezar en junio.»

feedback.es: Con un verbo de reporte en pasado, can retrocede a could.

hint.es: El verbo retrocede un paso: can cambia de forma.

origin.text: They asked me if I ___ start in June.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué defecto tiene el informe de Sam.

choices.text: It changes the question: yes or no becomes why.
It exaggerates the question.
It is faithful to the original.

feedback.es: La pregunta original es de sí o no (Can you…?) y Sam la cuenta como una pregunta de motivo (why). Cambia el tipo de pregunta.

origin.audio: Interviewer: Can you start next week? Later, Sam told his father: They asked me why I wanted to start next week.

prompt.es: Original: «¿Puedes trabajar los fines de semana?» Relaciona cada informe.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked why I work at weekends.
They asked whether I could work at weekends.

feedback.es: Solo el último informe conserva intención, contenido y grado. Los otros exageran, omiten o cambian el tipo de pregunta.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked why I work at weekends.
They asked whether I could work at weekends.

choices.text: They asked what I will do when the team disagrees.
They asked what I would do if the team disagreed.
They asked why the team disagreed.

feedback.es: La hipótesis se conserva con would + if + pasado. Will y when la convierten en un hecho seguro, y why cambia la pregunta.

origin.text: Original question: What would you do if the team disagreed?

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué defecto tiene el informe.

choices.text: It changes the question into an order.
It is faithful to the original.
It leaves out the condition about the morning.

feedback.es: La pregunta original tiene una condición (only in the morning) que el informe omite.

origin.audio: Panel: Can you work on Saturdays, but only in the morning? Report: They asked if I could work on Saturdays.

prompt.es: ¿Qué informe es fiel a la petición original?

choices.text: They asked me to describe a problem I had solved.
They asked whether I had a problem.
They challenged me about a problem I had solved.

feedback.es: La petición se conserva con asked me to + verbo. Las otras dos cambian a una pregunta de sí o no o a un cuestionamiento.

origin.text: Panel: Tell me about a problem you solved.

prompt.es: Completa el informe: «cuál era», «había trabajado», «qué haría».

feedback.es: En el informe el verbo retrocede: is pasa a was, have worked a had worked y will a would.

sentences: She asked me what my experience ___.
He asked how long I ___ worked there.
They asked what I ___ do if the team failed.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me preguntaron por qué había dejado mi trabajo anterior.»

answer.text: They asked me why I had left my last job

feedback.es: La pregunta con why se cuenta sin inversión y con el verbo retrocedido: why I had left.

choices.text: Yes, it keeps the same question.
No, it changes why into a yes or no question.
No, it exaggerates the question.

feedback.es: El original pregunta por el motivo (Why…?) y el informe pregunta si está interesado: cambia el tipo de pregunta.

origin.text: Original: Why are you interested in this school? Report: They asked me if I was interested in the school.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide si el informe de Ana es fiel.

choices.text: No, it changes the tense badly.
No, it leaves out the manager.
Yes, it keeps the hypothetical question.

feedback.es: Ana conserva la hipótesis (would… if… disagreed) y el tema (my manager). El informe es fiel.

origin.audio: Interviewer: What would you do if you disagreed with your manager? Later, Ana said: They asked what I would do if I disagreed with my manager.

prompt.es: Completa: «El comité quiso insistir pidiéndole más detalles.»

feedback.es: Press añade insistencia: pedir otra vez, con más fuerza, más detalles.

origin.text: The panel wanted to ___ him for more details.
